report.headline: Usage projected to drop from 23.5% in the EuroLeague to 18.1% in the NBA, while the shooting-efficiency projection carries no real signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 18.1% in the NBA, down from 23.5% in the EuroLeague (+0.71 sd above the EL average that season), against an NBA average of 20.0% (sd 5.2%).

risks.text: Projected usage of 18.1% falls below the NBA average of 20.0% and well below the 23.7% a pure standing-preservation baseline would predict, reflecting a fitted carry-over slope of only 0.579 for usage between these leagues.

Projected true shooting of 53.2% sits below the NBA average of 56.0%, but this projection is unreliable: the model's error (4.7%) is tied with just guessing the league mean, so the direction and size of this gap should not be trusted.

The historical cohort informing this transition is modest (61 EL->NBA transitions), and those movers sat only +0.46 sd above their own league on average, notably less than this player's own +0.71 sd standing, adding extrapolation risk to the projection.

strengths.text: Strong facilitation for the role: 5.285 assists per 75 possessions and a 25.4% assist rate alongside a low 12.5% turnover rate in the source season.
Carried a heavy offensive role in the EuroLeague, with a 23.5% usage rate sitting +0.71 sd above the league average.
Productive scoring line in the source season at 15.626 points per 75 possessions on a 55.2% true shooting percentage.
High reliance on the three-point shot (38.5% of attempts), consistent with a perimeter-oriented offensive profile.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 12.9% to 23.3%, a span of roughly two full standard deviations of NBA usage (sd 5.2%), and the 95% interval widens to 10.1%-26.1% — enough to rank this player against peers but not to price an individual outcome. The true-shooting projection (53.2%, interval 47.4%-59.0% at 80%) should not be read as informative at all: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league mean (4.7%).
